morning.title: Unvaccinated Pennsylvania woman died of measles complications, coroner says
morning.text:
A 40-year-old woman in Jefferson County, Pennsylvania has died of complications from measles, according to the county's coroner.

It marks the third vaccine-preventable, measles-linked death in the US this year. All three have occurred in Pennsylvania, which is experiencing an explosive outbreak that has caused over 670 cases and 124 hospitalizations across 37 counties. Prior to these deaths, Pennsylvania had not reported a measles death in 35 years.

In a news release dated September 12, Jefferson County Coroner Greg Furlong said the death in the woman was "a heartbreaking loss for the family and an unfortunate reminder that measles can be a serious and potentially life-threatening disease."

Interest extends beyond Pawan Hans to BSF, state governments, and Southeast Asian countries, alongside heli-tourism prospects.
Hindustan Aeronautics Limited is undertaking a major expansion into the civil aviation market. This strategy includes supplying aircraft and helicopters to civilian operators as part of its broader diversification beyond military contracts.
Hindustan Aeronautics Limited (HAL) is set to deliver four Dhruv NG helicopters to Pawan Hans. These helicopters form the first tranche of a larger order placed earlier in the year. The delivery represents a key milestone in HAL’s civil aviation expansion. The Dhruv NG is equipped with crashworthy seats designed to protect occupants during impact and self-sealing fuel tanks to reduce the risk of post-crash fires. These features enhance survivability in the event of an accident.
Pawan Hans intends to use the Dhruv NG helicopters for offshore operations in support of Oil and Natural Gas Corporation (ONGC). The planned operations will be conducted between Mumbai and Bombay High starting in the 2026–27 period.

morning.title: DRDO Completes Integration Trials of Indigenous Radome for Tejas Mk1A
morning.text:
Defence Research and Development Organisation (DRDO) has made another significant achievement in the development of an indigenous radome for Light Combat Aircraft (LCA) Tejas Mk1A. As per DRDO annual report prototype radome has been realised and integration trial with aircraft completed in May 2025.
The development is noteworthy for India’s indigenisation of the fighter aircraft program, as a radome is an essential part of the fighter’s radar and electromagnetic-sensor system. A radome is a specially-designed radome enclosure fastened to an aircraft’s radar antenna. It protects the antenna from aerodynamic loads, weather, dust, moisture and other environmental effects without prohibiting the passage of electromagnetic energy.
A radome can’t be a simple nose section from an aircraft, it needs to be designed and constructed from special material and structure. Reflections, absorption and distortion of any kind may adversely affect the performance of the radar, especially in precise tracking and long-range detection operations.The accurate transmission and reception of electromagnetic signals are vital to modern fighter radars. A loss or distortion of any magnitude by the radome can cause loss of radar efficiency, loss of beam steering and loss of performance in target detection.
The radome must therefore have to retain its structural strength without affecting the electromagnetic properties of the radar. This is more challenging when the aircraft is flying fast, in varying temperatures and in bad weather.According to the annual report, the prototype radome was created and then installed in the aircraft for testing in May 2025.
The purpose of an integration trial is to test the fit of the radome with the aircraft’s nose structure and installation of the radar. It can also be used to evaluate problems arising out of alignment, mounting, structural compatibility, airflow and the interaction of the radome with the radar antenna.

morning.title: HQ IDS to Organise ‘CORE’ Programme on Contemporary Security Challenges and National Security
morning.text:
HQ Integrated Defence Staff (IDS) is organising ‘Combined Operational Review and Evaluation (CORE)’ programme from 14 to 18 September 2026 at Manekshaw Centre, New Delhi, for senior officers of the Defence Forces. Officers from the Ministries of Defence, External Affairs and Home Affairs are also participating in the five-day programme.
The CORE programme aims to provide senior leaders with exposure to contemporary national and regional security issues through interactions with distinguished subject matter experts and renowned speakers from diverse fields. The programme will facilitate a deeper understanding of emerging challenges and enable participants to take balanced and well-informed decisions in their future leadership roles.
The five-day programme will cover a wide spectrum of themes, including emerging regional and global security challenges, technological transformation in warfare, strategic communication, and the need for enhanced civil-military understanding in addressing complex issues.
The programme reflects the commitment of HQ Integrated Defence Staff towards strengthening professional competencies, fostering jointness and integrated thinking, and preparing senior leadership to effectively address the dynamic and evolving challenges of national security.
